text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- An attack on a journalist in Ankara's pro-Islamist Sincan district caused tension throughout Turkey.

- The Islamist prime minister, Necmettin Erbakan, is gearing up to pass a decree lifting a ban on the Islamic headscarf in universities and the civil service with only the approval of his coalition partner Tansu Ciller -- bypassing other ministers of Ciller's conservative party.
- The provacations by the Islamists mount as Erbakan promises to implement his radical pre-election promises.
- MPs are searching for a coalition government formula that does not include Erbakan's Welfare Party, the biggest party in the house.
- The radical Islamist Hizbullah organisation has killed 225 people in southeastern Turkey over the past five years.
- The monthly inflation rate for January is expected to be lower than last year's figure.
- The foreign ministry warns Iran's ambassador to Ankara over his calling for the Islamic Sharia law in Turkey during a night organised by an Islamist munipicality in Ankara.
